intro: Private investigators solve puzzles, read people and document facts that stand up later. The closest of the 25 careers below is Detectives and Criminal Investigators, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $93,790, which is 83% more than the $51,220 private investigators earn.
why_it_works: An investigation means planning surveillance, interviewing people who may not want to talk and writing reports that hold up in court. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.75 out of 5 for this job and social perceptiveness at 3.5. Fraud, compliance and legal support roles use the same strengths. Some need a bachelor's degree. The gaps include teaching others, quality checks and leading teams.
tips: Specialize: fraud, insurance and corporate cases translate directly into compliance and fraud examiner jobs.
Paralegals and Legal Assistants earn $62,890, which is 23% more, and value your report writing.
Ask local police departments whether investigative experience counts toward detective requirements.

faq.q: What jobs can former private investigators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are detectives and criminal investigators (88%), fraud examiners and analysts (85%) and Compliance Officers (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Compliance Officers earn $80,730, which is 58% more than the $51,220 private investigator median, though many employers want a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Which careers for private investigators pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more. Management Analysts earn $101,860 (99% more), detectives and criminal investigators $93,790 (83% more) and Compliance Officers $80,730 (58% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Compliance Managers earn $141,900 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Do private investigators need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Sometimes. 19 of the 25 matches need no more education than private investigators already have, but only 6 of the top 10 do. Many investigation roles expect a professional certification or license, and fraud and compliance jobs often ask for a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: What skills should private investigators build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, quality control analysis, managing people and coordination. Judgment already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading a team and checking others' work are the main steps up.
